name: Takebashi
tagline: Otemachi in 2 minutes and Tokyo in 8 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥140,000 to ¥150,000.
summary: The station is in Chiyoda City, where Tokyo Metro run 1 line between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 2 minutes to Otemachi, 18 minutes to Shinjuku, 21 minutes to Shibuya and 23 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥140,000 to ¥150,000. The station stands 4.6 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 16.7 m. The land around the station has gentle slopes.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 4.6 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 3.6 m to 20.3 m, a difference of 16.7 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls outside the projected inundation area. Even so, 3 of the nine points within 400 m fall inside the area, and the deepest projection there is 0.5 to 3 m. For storm surge, 2 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the small side for the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 10 clinics and 12 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 宮内庁病院, about 9 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 九段坂病院, about 9 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Tokyo Metro Tozai Line.
congestion: Tokyo Metro Tozai Line runs at 160% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 木場→門前仲町, which this station is not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥140,000 to ¥150,000 and 1K ¥140,000 to ¥150,000. 1LDK ¥210,000 to ¥220,000 and 2LDK ¥700,000 to ¥710,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.
drivers: Age and construction of the building
Whether it faces a main road or the railway
Whether it sits at the top or the bottom of a slope

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥140,000 to ¥150,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is among the highest in the 23 wards. For 1LDK, 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: For rail connections, Jimbocho; for how little of the area is in the flood projection, Takebashi.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Takebashi. Jimbocho also has the Tokyo Metro Hanzomon Line, Toei Mita Line and Toei Shinjuku Line, which Takebashi does not. With more lines, Jimbocho is the better connected of the two. To Shinjuku, for instance, Jimbocho is 5 minutes quicker. On how little of the area is in the flood projection, though, Takebashi comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: For rail connections, Kudanshita; for lower rent, Takebashi.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Takebashi. Kudanshita also has the Tokyo Metro Hanzomon Line and Toei Shinjuku Line, which Takebashi does not. With more lines, Kudanshita is the better connected of the two. To Shinjuku, for instance, Kudanshita is 7 minutes quicker. A one-room flat, though, costs about ¥5,000 more at Kudanshita.

goodFor: People commuting to Otemachi and Marunouchi
notFor: People who want another route when service is suspended
People who want to finish their shopping on foot
noiseSources: The 首都高速都心環状線 viaduct runs right beside the station. It is an expressway, so traffic is audible day and night
内堀通り (4 lanes each way) runs right beside the station. Traffic on it never stops, so for a flat close to the station, check whether it faces the road

leads.terrain: There are gentle slopes around the station, and which block you live on changes how much effort getting about takes.
leads.groceries: There are 3 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 8 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself is outside the projected flood area, but blocks nearby are inside it.
leads.stationNote: Only the Tokyo Metro Tozai Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are among the highest in the 23 wards.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is on the high side for the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are heavily loaded in the morning.
leads.noiseSources: At this station, check the traffic noise before the noise people make.
